summary: The change is not a repeat, breaks no promise or mechanism, and every number the planner cites reproduces exactly - but its headline story (put the review ask at the 'payoff moment' and it will convert) is contradicted by the funnel's own data: the surfaces that ARE at the true payoff (preview/share, seen after the video is watched) already produce ~0 clicks, while the one working ask is a captive full-screen interstitial the user is parked on, not a payoff. Build it for its real, defensible value - adding tracking and a correct-per-product ASIN to a live surface that has neither - but first correct the conversion narrative to honest expectations and verify the ASIN-resolution dependency, or the 'correct ASIN' benefit silently degrades to routing every non-potato buyer to the potato listing.

findings.issue: The assumed cause (H4: the working ask works because it is at the payoff moment, so a payoff-moment email ask will convert) is contradicted by the plan's own within-funnel evidence. The ask that works (in_app thankyou, 10/10 clicks this window) fires BEFORE the user has seen the video (email-first flow) - the plan itself calls this 'anticipation, not payoff'. The surfaces at the ACTUAL payoff (preview/share, shown after the user watches the finished video) produce ~0 clicks. So payoff-timing is not what drives review clicks; the thankyou more likely works because it is a captive, full-screen, nothing-else-to-do interstitial ('leave a review while you wait', index.html line 1974) during the 60-120s generation wait. The proposed surface is a SECONDARY link placed below a primary 'Watch & Share' CTA, leading to video-preview.html - i.e. it structurally resembles the preview/share asks that already convert ~0, not the thankyou that works.
findings.evidence: funnel-report 14d ->2026-07-21 reran live: 10/10 review clicks from in_app thankyou (buyer 5, receiver 5), 0 from preview/share/email. Prior window: preview_receiver 3, thankyou 4, email_redirect 2. index.html line 1974 confirms the thankyou is the captive 'leave a review while you wait' screen. resolve-video.js sendVideoEmail (lines 185-187) links to video-preview.html - the same page whose June-reworked review card produces ~0 (coverage map).
findings.required_fix: Reframe expected_effect and choice_reasoning: do NOT sell this as a likely conversion win via payoff-timing. State the honest prior - a secondary link below the share CTA on the path to the ~0-converting preview page will most plausibly behave like preview/share (~0), and the durable, defensible value is (a) making the surface TRACKED for future cycles and (b) correct-per-product ASIN routing. Keep measurable:false (already correct).

findings.issue: The plan's central differentiator over the dead file - 'routes to the CORRECT per-product ASIN so reviews are verified-eligible and count' - depends on two things it flags but does not verify, and its 'graceful fallback' is not graceful: if sku is null on the row OR review-redirect cannot reach master_products, EVERY delivery-email review click 302s to the default ASIN B0DVR6VBRR (the potato). For a buyer of a cupcake / nurse-potato / dad-jokes product that is the WRONG listing, where they cannot leave a valid review - arguably worse than the status quo of no link at all.
findings.evidence: review-redirect.js line 44 defaultAsin='B0DVR6VBRR'; it currently accepts only {email, asin} (line 42) and does NOT query master_products, so the sku->asin lookup must be ADDED. product-lookup.js reads ROS_SUPABASE_* creds (master_products lives in the ROS project, not the crochet Supabase review-redirect uses today), and plan unverified_assumption #3 admits those env keys may not be configured in the deploy. sku IS forwarded from index.html line 1957 and stored on video_sessions (generate-video.js lines 89/143/251), so per-row population is usually OK for QR arrivals - but resolution failure is env-level and therefore wholesale.
findings.required_fix: Before relying on the correct-ASIN benefit, verify in the actual deploy that review-redirect can resolve sku->asin against master_products (ROS env reachable). If it cannot, either configure that env (report it as a deploy dependency) or drop the correct-ASIN claim. Do not ship a version whose only realistic behaviour is fallback-to-potato for non-potato buyers.

findings.issue: The plan says whether delivery-email openers are buyers (verified-review-eligible) or receivers 'cannot be determined from current data', but an adverse signal IS available and points against the plan's ceiling: the in-app role split is heavily receiver-weighted, and receivers who did not buy on Amazon cannot leave a verified-purchase review. This caps the upside of even a correctly-targeted ASIN for the majority audience.
findings.evidence: funnel-report role split (all events) this window: receiver 213, buyer 80, unknown 109 (~73% receiver among identified). Prior window: receiver 259, buyer 61. Video creators / email openers therefore skew strongly to the verified-ineligible group.
findings.required_fix: Acknowledge the receiver-heavy role split as an available (if imperfect, self-identified) headwind on the ceiling rather than claiming it is undeterminable; fold it into the honest expected-value framing above.

findings.issue: Reach is slightly overstated: 'opened by ~36 finishers/fortnight'. ~36 is videos completed (video_created=36) = emails SENT; opens are fewer, and the +20-40% (a few clicks) estimate sits on top of that and on the contradicted payoff-timing theory.
findings.evidence: funnel-report: video_created 36 = sends, not opens. review_clicked base = 10/fortnight. Any true effect is far inside the ~13-20pt noise floor regardless (plan correctly labels measurable:false).
findings.required_fix: Soften 'opened by ~36' to 'sent to ~36' and present the +20-40% as an optimistic ceiling, not an expectation. No blocker given measurable:false.
